section_04.text: Check that the energy really is concentrated at 1× shaft rate and that the 2× to 1× ratio is low. Imbalance is a once-per-revolution force, so a strong 2× component points at misalignment or looseness instead. (source: imbalance-1x; AI-drafted, not yet checked against a published source)

Check that the signal is smooth rather than impulsive. A low or negative excess kurtosis is consistent with imbalance; a strongly positive value suggests impacts and therefore a different cause. (source: imbalance-1x; AI-drafted, not yet checked against a published source)

Inspect the rotor for added, lost or displaced mass: fouling, debris, a missing balance weight, a damaged blade or vane, or moisture collected on one side. (source: imbalance-1x; AI-drafted, not yet checked against a published source)

Record again at a second shaft speed. The 1× amplitude from a mass imbalance rises steeply with speed, so a component that does not grow with speed is probably not imbalance. (source: imbalance-1x; AI-drafted, not yet checked against a published source)

Refer the residual imbalance to the balance-quality grade appropriate for the machine type before deciding whether correction is required. (source: imbalance-1x; AI-drafted, not yet checked against a published source)

items.text: Verdict: known fault: imbalance.

Decision rule: provisional research setting. The decision rule is a provisional setting, not a final rule selection; the final choice will be made later under stated assumptions about fault frequency and costs.
Location according to the dataset label: rotor discs.
Most probable classes (CNN-6 scores): imbalance > 0.9999, normal < 0.0001, underhang ball < 0.0001. Model scores are not the probability that the diagnosis is correct.
Classifier confidence (MSP) 0.999918 ≥ 0.998895: pass (margin +0.001023, +92.551 % on the 1 − MSP scale).
Familiarity (Mahalanobis distance) 6.3834 ≤ 30.04: pass (margin -23.66, -78.752 %).
Autoencoder error 0.560800 > 0.243072: above healthy limit — consistent with a fault (margin +0.3177, +130.714 %).
Speed-aware baseline (B1s) 1.8581 > 0.872143: above healthy limit — consistent with a fault (margin +0.986, +113.054 %).
Measured shaft speed 18.79 Hz (1128 rpm); speed stable within the recording (0.22 %).
overhang tangential: 1× amplitude ↑ ×11.7 vs the healthy training recording normal__20.2752, beyond the typical healthy variation (×2.3); descriptive, not a calibrated anomaly test.
overhang axial: RMS ↓ ×5.5 vs the healthy training recording normal__20.2752, beyond the typical healthy variation (×1.3); descriptive, not a calibrated anomaly test.

Secondary logistic regression (imbalance) leans on: amplitude at 4× the window's shaft speed (overhang axial) (+0.88); excess kurtosis (Fisher) of the window (underhang axial) (+0.56); amplitude at 4× the window's shaft speed (overhang radial) (+0.46).
This recording was used to build the model; the result is not evidence of accuracy.
No maintenance history, operating context or repeat recording is available.
The healthy baseline is calibrated on 5 healthy recordings from one folder.
